'''''Fritillaria pyrenaica''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the lily [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Liliaceae, [[native plant|native]] to the [[Pyrenees]] in [[Spain]] and [[France]].<ref name=botanica>Cheers, G. and H. F. Ullmann. ''Botanica: The Illustrated A-Z of Over 10,000 Garden Plants and how to Cultivate Them''. Könemann im Tandem. 2004. p. 384. {{ISBN|3-8331-1253-0}}</ref> Common names include '''Pyrenean fritillary'''<ref name=rhs>[https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/7429/Fritillaria-pyrenaica/Details ''Fritillaria pyrenaica''.] Royal Horticultural Society.</ref> and '''Pyrenean snake's-head'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> It is a [[bulb]]ous [[perennial plant|perennial]] growing to {{convert|45|cm|0|abbr=on}}. The pendent, bell-shaped flowers are borne in spring. They have recurved [[tepal]]s<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z Encyclopedia of Garden Plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> which are purple tinged with brown and yellow.<ref name=botanica/> Like other species in this genus, notably ''[[Fritillaria meleagris|F. meleagris]]'', they are strongly chequered.<ref name=RHSAZ/>

==Subspecies==
Two subspecies are currently recognized:<ref name="boxelder"/><ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=309502 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, 	Fritillaria pyrenaica subsp. boissieri]</ref>

''Fritillaria pyrenaica'' subsp. ''boissieri'' <small>(Costa) Vigo & Valdés</small><ref>Vigo Bonada, Josep & Valdés, Benito. 2004. Willdenowia 34: 64.</ref>

''Fritillaria pyrenaica'' subsp. ''pyrenaica''

==Cultivation==
In cultivation in the [[UK]] ''Fritillaria pyrenaica'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=rhs/><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 39 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 27 February 2018}}</ref> It grows in any open place, such as a flower border or meadow, in full sun. Like all the Liliaceae, it is subject to predation by the [[scarlet lily beetle]] and its larvae.<ref name = rhs/>
